days.title: Caldera and Central Peaks
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Askja
stops.detail: The caldera of Askja is also located within it.

stops.name: Þorvaldstindur
stops.detail: The highest peak is the Þorvaldstindur with a height of 1,510 m.

stops.name: Jónsskarð
stops.detail: Also one of the passes between the peaks, Jónsskarð, is named after an Icelandic geologist, namely after Jón Þorkelsson, who was the first to describe the volcano Askja.

days.title: Eastern Passages and Lake
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Öskjuop
stops.detail: The lowest-lying pass between these mountains, which simultaneously form the rim of the Askja caldera, is the Öskjuop.

stops.name: Öskjuvatn
stops.detail: Here the caldera (German for "Askja") opens to the east and through it a hiking trail also leads to the lake Öskjuvatn.

stops.name: Drekagil
stops.detail: Also to the east of it lies a gorge called Dragon Gorge (Icelandic: Drekagil).

days.title: Valleys and Mountain Huts
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Dyngjudalur
stops.detail: On the western side, the valley Dyngjudalur cuts into the mountains, so that one speaks here of the Vestari-Dyngjufjöll.

stops.name: Dreki
stops.detail: There is a hut, Dreki, belonging to the Akureyri Hiking Association.

stops.name: Dyngjufjöll-Hütte
stops.detail: This hiking association also operates the Dyngjufjöll Hut, which is located north-northwest of Askja.
